summary: A queued folder whose open fails with 2 or 3 while the scan root still opens is now counted in a new ScanResult.FoldersVanished. It is not stamped or recorded unreadable, and it finishes as a listed empty folder. If the root does not open either (letter removed, share dropped, root deleted), the folder stays unreadable as before, which is what review M1 asked for. The ending says it in one new note, and the report carries core.foldersVanished. The whole suite passes (1346, up from 1260) and the SL-005 repro now exits 0. The published app in report mode, with three queued folders deleted, gave foldersVanished 3, unreadable 0, the note, no 'missing' captions and the Unreadable tab hidden. The note's line sits in the outcome texts, which are capped at 76 px against an extent of 97 px, so it may be a scroll away. That is the layout every other note already has.

Measured on a SUBST letter the test makes and removes itself: the queued folders and the root both fail to open, and before the check all three queued folders were counted deleted. FolderDone now opens the scan root once (_reader.Open with keepLastAccess false, closed again). If it does not open, the folder stays unreadable. A Stop aborting that open returns before anything is committed, so nothing is stamped or counted and the scan ends Cancelled. SubstDrive is shared and picks and maps under one lock.

The builder now owns the material checks: VanishedFolderTests asserts row y's UnreadableBelow 0 and no flag on w (code 3), the Deny control and the ScanFailingPartway control. The App side is tests/window/SL-005-VanishedFolders.Tests.ps1, listed as not-a-launcher in AppArgumentCorpus.json. Its tree puts z1 to z3 after a 50,201-folder subtree under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. The deletion is timed from the app's start, and the verdict comes from core.folders: exactly base+3 means it landed, base or less is INCONCLUSIVE-EARLY, base+6 is INCONCLUSIVE-LATE, a partial landing is INCONCLUSIVE, each retried at most twice with the delay moved the right way. Case C pins all 12 endings.

architecture.why: Scanner.cs FolderVanished, GoneGivenRootOpen and RootOpenError, used in Run.FolderDone; ScanResult.FoldersVanished set in Finish.

deviations: Review M1's critic prescribed that an aborted root check stamps nothing and counts nothing and that FolderDone's final return then ends the scan Cancelled. I return from FolderDone before SetChildren in that case, so the folder stays NotListed as any Stop-cut folder does, not listed-empty. This keeps the established rule that an aborted call commits nothing. VanishedFolderTests.AStopInTheRootCheckStampsNothingAndCountsNothing pins it for a cancel before and during the call.

Review M1 offered a [Collection] with DisableParallelization or a retry for the SUBST race. I took neither: SubstDrive is one shared helper whose letter pick and subst.exe call run under a static lock. All test classes run in one process, so the lock closes the race without serialising ContainerLayerStoreTests with the rest of the suite.

The design's FolderVanished(error, opened) is as specified; the root check is a second pure predicate, GoneGivenRootOpen(rootOpenError), and RootOpenError() in Run. The design did not have them; review M1 required the root check.

No workaround checkbox or KnownWorkarounds entry: the classification is this project's own, and the root check guards against the OS answering 2 or 3 for a path that stopped resolving, which is the app's own heuristic. Nothing outside the project is worked around.

The design's planted E007* finish-line tests do not exist in the tree (lessons #876, #888, #896). Review M2 handed their cases to the builder, so the material checks are VanishedFolderTests and tests/window/SL-005-VanishedFolders.Tests.ps1.
not_built: Delete-pending folders (open fails with 5) and folders replaced by a file (listing 87) stay unreadable, as the design decided. The NTSTATUS split and the handle check are not built.
No per-folder 'deleted' mark in the folder tree or results list and no live 'deleted' counter: only the ending's count and note, as designed.

Exit codes 2 and 70 and the throw-mode, missing-value and unwritable-path runs are not re-checked in the new window script; review M2's prescription left them to the existing cases. This script checks exit 0 and the schema-1 keys.
follow_ups: At a finished ending the outcome texts are capped at 76 px while the tabs show (measured here: actualHeight 76, extentHeight 97.12), so the new note, like the files-vanished and probe-failure notes, can sit a scroll away. The layout is not this slice's. It is worth its own slice if the notes should be seen without scrolling.

Check on an SMB share (the loopback rig), a DFS link whose target is down, ReFS and FAT/exFAT that a queued folder deleted mid-scan reaches core.foldersVanished and that a folder still there but unreachable never does. This is the design's filed item for a person and O-002. The root check makes a dropped share stay unreadable, but its codes were measured only on SUBST and local NTFS.
W-001 and W-003 verdicts do not read the ending's notes (review M1's remark). A cut share now keeps its unreadable rows, but a later slice could have Get-ShareVerdict read the notes.

Ending text and the walk changed under src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning and src/FsAnalyser.App, so the C:\ and OneDrive proof runs and the network pass go stale under the project's rule. The runs come after E-007, E-006 and E-005 per Q-016, so this changes nothing about their order.
